questions.question: The marked price of a bookshelf is ₹3,100, which is 25% above the cost price. It is sold at a discount of 12% on the marked price. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹3,100

Cost Price (CP) = ?

Discount = 12%

Marked Price is 25% above the Cost Price.

**Formula used:**

1. MP = CP × (1 + 25/100)

2. Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 - Discount/100)

3. Profit Percentage = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100

**Calculation:**

MP = CP × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ ₹3,100 = CP × (1.25)

⇒ CP = ₹3,100 / 1.25

⇒ CP = ₹2,480

SP = MP × (1 - Discount/100)

⇒ SP = ₹3,100 × (1 - 12/100)

⇒ SP = ₹3,100 × 0.88

⇒ SP = ₹2,728

Profit Percentage = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = [(₹2,728 - ₹2,480)/₹2,480] × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = [₹248/₹2,480] × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 0.1 × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: The mode and median of a dataset is 52.7 and 65, respectively. What is the mean of the dataset? (Use empirical formula, and round off your answer to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mode = 52.7

Median = 65

**Formula Used:**

Empirical formula: Mean - Mode = 3 × (Mean - Median)

**Calculations:**

Mean - 52.7 = 3 × (Mean - 65)

⇒ Mean - 52.7 = 3 × Mean - 3 × 65

⇒ Mean - 52.7 = 3 × Mean - 195

⇒ 195 - 52.7 = 3 × Mean - Mean

⇒ 142.3 = 2 × Mean

⇒ Mean = 142.3 / 2

⇒ Mean = 71.15

⇒ Mean ≈ 71.2

The **mean** of the dataset is **71.2**.

questions.question:
Find the volume (in cm³) of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube with an edge of 8 cm.

Use pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Edge of the cube = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

For the largest right circular cone cut from a cube:

Diameter of the base of the cone = Edge of the cube

Height of the cone = Edge of the cube

Volume of a cone = 1/3 × π × r² × h

Where, r = radius, h = height

**Calculations:**

Diameter of the cone = 8 cm

⇒ Radius (r) = 8/2 = 4 cm

Height (h) = 8 cm

Volume of the cone = 1/3 × (22/7) × 4² × 8

⇒ Volume of the cone = 1/3 × (22/7) × 16 × 8

⇒ Volume of the cone = (22 × 16 × 8) / (3 × 7)

⇒ Volume of the cone = 2816 / 21

⇒ Volume of the cone ≈ 134(2)/(21) cm³

**∴ The volume of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube with an edge of 8 cm is **134(2)/(21)** **cm3

questions.question: What is the average of the first 10 prime numbers?

questions.question: The sides (in cm) of a right triangle are (x − 13), (x − 26) and x. Its area (in cm²) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sides of right triangle: (x − 13), (x − 26), and x cm

**Formula used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Height²

Area = (1/2) × Base × Height

**Calculation:**

Hypotenuse = x, Base = (x - 26), Height = (x - 13)

Assume hypotenuse = x

⇒ x² = (x − 13)² + (x − 26)²

⇒ x² = (x² − 26x + 169) + (x² − 52x + 676)

⇒ x² = 2x² − 78x + 845

⇒ Bring all terms to one side:

⇒ x² − 2x² + 78x − 845 = 0

⇒ −x² + 78x − 845 = 0

⇒ x² − 78x + 845 = 0

Solve using quadratic formula:

x = [78 ± √(78² − 4 × 1 × 845)] ÷ 2

x = [78 ± √(6084 − 3380)] ÷ 2

x = [78 ± √2704] ÷ 2

x = [78 ± 52] ÷ 2

⇒ x = (78 + 52)/2 = 130 ÷ 2 = 65 (valid)

⇒ x = (78 − 52)/2 = 26 ÷ 2 = 13 (invalid as sides become 0)

If x = 13, then one side is (x - 13) = (13 - 13) = 0, which is not possible for a triangle. So, x ≠ 13.

So, x = 65

Now, find the lengths of the sides:

Side 1 = x - 13 = 65 - 13 = 52 cm

Side 2 = x - 26 = 65 - 26 = 39 cm

Hypotenuse = x = 65 cm

Area = (1/2) × 39 × 52 = 1014 cm²

**∴ Area = 1014 cm²**

questions.question: If 68 is the mean proportion between x and 272, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mean proportion = 68

x = Unknown

Second term = 272

**Formula used:**

If 68 is the mean proportion between x and 272, the formula used is:

Mean proportion = √(x × 272)

**Calculation:**

68 = √(x × 272)

⇒ 68² = x × 272

⇒ 4624 = x × 272

⇒ x = 4624 ÷ 272

⇒ x = 17

questions.question: Manoj has 200 litres of Oil A and 274 litres of Oil B. He fills a number of identical containers with the two types of oil in a manner that each container has only one type of oil, and all containers are completely filled. What can be the maximum volume (in litres) of each container that Manoj uses, so that all the oil that Manoj has, of both the types, can be poured into these containers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Volume of Oil A = 200 litres

Volume of Oil B = 274 litres

**Formula used:**

The maximum volume of each container = HCF (Highest Common Factor) of the volumes of Oil A and Oil B.

**Calculation:**

Find HCF of 200 and 274:

Prime factorization of 200 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5

Prime factorization of 274 = 2 × 137

Common factor = 2

⇒ HCF = 2

**∴ The maximum volume of each container is 2 litres.**

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest, compounded annually and the simple interest if ₹17,700 is deposited at 4% rate of interest per annum for 2 years is:

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × r × t) / 100

Compound Interest (CI) = P × (1 + r/100)t - P

Difference between CI and SI = CI - SI

**Calculations:**

Simple Interest (SI):

SI = (17700 × 4 × 2) / 100

⇒ SI = (141600) / 100

⇒ SI = ₹1,416

Compound Interest (CI):

CI = 17700 × (1 + 4/100)² - 17700

⇒ CI = 17700 × (1.04)² - 17700

⇒ CI = 17700 × 1.0816 - 17700

⇒ CI = 19144.32 - 17700

⇒ CI = ₹1,444.32

Difference between CI and SI:

Difference = CI - SI

⇒ Difference = 1444.32 - 1416

⇒ Difference = ₹28.32

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A man has to cover a distance of 387 km in 21 hours. If he covers two - thirds of this distance in 5/7 of the time, then what should his speed (in km/hr) be to cover the remaining distance in the time left ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 387 km

Total time = 21 hours

**Formula used:**

Remaining distance = Total − Covered

Remaining time = Total time − Time used

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

Distance covered = 2/3 of 387 = 258 km

Time used = 5/7 of 21 = 15 hours

⇒ Remaining distance = 387 − 258 = 129 km

⇒ Remaining time = 21 − 15 = 6 hours

⇒ Required speed = 129 ÷ 6 = 21.5 km/h

**∴ Required speed = 21.5 km/h**

questions.question: The average of 10 observations is 40. It was realised later that an observation was misread as 33 in place of 50. Find the correct average.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 10 observations = 40

Total of 10 observations = 40 × 10 = 400

Incorrect observation = 33

Correct observation = 50

**Formula used:**

Correct Total = Incorrect Total - Incorrect Observation + Correct Observation

Correct Average = Correct Total ÷ Number of Observations

**Calculations:**

Total with incorrect data = 400

⇒ Correct Total = 400 - 33 + 50

⇒ Correct Total = 417

⇒ Correct Average = 417 ÷ 10

⇒ Correct Average = 41.7

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 21 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 24 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Filling pipe time = 21 min

Emptying pipe time = 24 min

Target = 1/4 of tank

Calculation:

LCM method: Assume tank capacity = LCM of 21 and 24 = 168 units

Filling rate = 168 ÷ 21 = 8 units/min

Emptying rate = 168 ÷ 24 = 7 units/min

Net rate = 8 − 7 = 1 unit/min

⇒ 1/4 of 168 = 168 ÷ 4 = 42 units

⇒ Time = 42 ÷ 1 = 42 min

**∴ Time to fill 1/4 tank = 42 minutes**

questions.question: If tan theta = (7)/(8) , then evaluate ((1 + sin theta)(1 - sin theta))/((1 + cos theta)(1 - cos theta)(cot theta))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

tantheta = (7)/(8)

Expression to evaluate: dfrac{(1 + sintheta)(1 - sintheta)}{(1 + costheta)(1 - costheta)(cottheta)}

**Formula used:**

1. (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b²

2. sin²theta + cos²theta = 1

⇒ 1 - sin²theta = cos²theta

⇒ 1 - cos²theta = sin²theta

3. cottheta = dfrac{costheta}{sintheta}

4. cottheta = dfrac{1}{tantheta}

**Calculations:**

Simplify the numerator:

Numerator = (1 + sintheta)(1 - sintheta)

⇒ Numerator = 1² - sin²theta

⇒ Numerator = 1 - sin²theta

⇒ Numerator = cos²theta

Simplify the denominator:

Denominator = (1 + costheta)(1 - costheta)(cottheta)

⇒ Denominator = (1² - cos²theta)(cottheta)

⇒ Denominator = (1 - cos²theta)(cottheta)

⇒ Denominator = sin²theta times cottheta

Substitute cottheta = dfrac{costheta}{sintheta}:

⇒ Denominator = sin²theta times dfrac{costheta}{sintheta}

⇒ Denominator = sintheta costheta

Now, substitute the simplified numerator and denominator into the expression:

Expression = dfrac{cos²theta}{sintheta costheta}

Cancel out costheta from numerator and denominator:

⇒ Expression = dfrac{costheta}{sintheta}

⇒ Expression = cottheta

Given tantheta = dfrac{7}{8}.

Since cottheta = dfrac{1}{tantheta}:

⇒ Expression = dfrac{1}{(7)/(8)}

⇒ Expression = dfrac{8}{7}

**∴ The value of the expression is dfrac{8}{7}.**

ABCD is a trapezium in which BC ∥ AD and AC = CD. If ∠ABC = 69° and ∠BAC = 23° , then what is the measure of ∠ACD (in degree) .?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f6df85bb678d4030b9f025ad2b98108a24cc1b9378ff5943eebe2ebcbe93d04f.png] **

In Δ ABC:

∠ACB = 180° - (∠ABC + ∠BAC) = 180° - (69° + 23°) = 180° - 92° = 88°

Since AD ∥ BC,

So, ∠ACB = ∠CAD = 88°

Now, In Δ ACD:

AC = CD, So ∠CAD = ∠ADC

i.e. ∠CAD = ∠ADC = 88°

So, ∠ACD = 180 - (∠CAD + ∠ADC)

⇒ 180° - (88° + 88°) = 180° - 176° = 4°

questions.question: X, Y and Z invest a sum in the ratio 6 : 59 : 41 respectively. If they earned total profit of ₹3,180 at the end of year, then what is the difference between the share of Y and Z?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total profit = ₹3,180

Investment ratio of X : Y : Z = 6 : 59 : 41

**Formula used:**

Profit share = (Individual investment ratio / Total ratio) × Total profit

**Calculation:**

Total ratio = 6 + 59 + 41 = 106

Profit share of Y = (59 / 106) × 3180

⇒ Profit share of Y = ₹1,770

Profit share of Z = (41 / 106) × 3180

⇒ Profit share of Z = ₹1,230

Difference between share of Y and Z = ₹1,770 - ₹1,230

⇒ Difference = ₹540

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
